title: Fully faithful functors lift isomorphisms uniquely
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories [def-nagata-category] in fixed universes, and let $A:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor that is fully faithful, meaning that its map on each set of morphisms is bijective. For every $U,V\in\mathcal C$, the map
$$\operatorname{Iso}_{\mathcal C}(U,V)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Iso}_{\mathcal D}(AU,AV),\qquad u\longmapsto A(u)$$
is a bijection. In particular every specified isomorphism $v:AU\xrightarrow{\sim}AV$ has a unique isomorphism $u:U\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ with $A(u)=v$.
